puzzles.security_scope: Adapted port of insertion_sort_by_keys only, with an explicit strict two-tree-argument module wrapper. The first input is not presorted or fully validated. Empty insertions return any sorted tree unchanged; an empty sorted tree can accept a malformed single entry without reading its key. Comparisons require atom keys and use unsigned lexicographic byte order, preserving padding, arbitrary payloads and any unvisited improper tail. Equal-key placement is stable when the initial list is descending; no stability guarantee is added for unsorted input. Nonempty zero atoms are not nil. Malformed paths reject only when visited. This is finite helper evidence, not verification of the enclosing credential proof checker, a protocol, a canonical module hash, authorization, constant-time behavior or compiler preservation.

  (defmacro assert items
    (if (r items)
        (list if (f items) (c assert (r items)) (q . (x)))
        (f items)

  (defmacro and ARGS
    (if ARGS
        (qq (if (unquote (f ARGS))
                (unquote (c and (r ARGS)))
                ()
        ))
    1)
  )

  (defmacro or ARGS
    (if ARGS
        (qq (if (unquote (f ARGS))
                1
                (unquote (c or (r ARGS)))
        ))
    0)
  )

  (defun in (atom list_a)
    (if list_a
        (i (= atom (f list_a))
          1
          (in atom (r list_a))
        )
        ()
    )
  )

  (defun gte (atom_a atom_b)
    (not (> atom_b atom_a))
  )

  (defun lte (atom_a atom_b)
    (not (> atom_a atom_b))

puzzles.security_scope: The raw tutorial module receives PASSWORD_HASH, password and conditions through the first three pair projections, then ignores any remaining tail. It returns the exact conditions tree only when SHA256(password atom bytes) equals the expected hash atom bytes. An uncurried attacker can choose both hash and password.
